prompt: A storage tank is being filled by a pipe at a rate of 15 liters per minute while a leak drains it at 4 liters per minute. If the tank currently holds 200 liters and its capacity is 500 liters, calculate how many minutes it will take to reach full capacity.
evaluation_criteria:
Net Rate Calculation: 0-5 (Evaluates correct net fill rate computation)
Time To Capacity: 0-5 (Evaluates correct division of remaining volume by net rate)
response_text:
The net rate at which the tank is gaining water is the difference between the inflow and the leak:

\[
\text{Net rate} = 15\ \text{L/min} - 4\ \text{L/min} = 11\ \text{L/min}.
\]

The tank currently holds \(200\) L and must reach its capacity of \(500\) L, so it needs:

\[
500\ \text{L} - 200\ \text{L} = 300\ \text{L}
\]

more water.

Time required:

\[
\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Volume needed}}{\text{Net rate}} = \frac{300\ \text{L}}{11\ \text{L/min}} \approx 27.27\ \text{minutes}.
\]

**Result:** It will take about **27.3 minutes** (≈ 27 minutes 16 seconds) for the tank to become full.
